card: Adds an optional `txoscriptindex` and a `getscripthistory` RPC supporting scripts, addresses, and ranged descriptors. Bitcoin Core does not index transaction history by script or address, forcing users to run third-party indexers or Electrum servers to serve external wallets. Address-based indexing has been requested across at least five previous pull requests dating back to 2013; the author reports this design syncs in a few hours and requires approximately 61 GB of disk space.
evidence: Address-based indexing has been requested and attempted repeatedly in closed PRs #2802, #3652, #6835, #10370, and #14053.

Author provides performance measurements: 'This index can be synced in a few hours and the current disk usage is ~61 GB. This is less than the ~66 GB txindex disk usage in v31 and earlier. This index can also be used with a pruned node, so a full node can be supported in < 100 GB of disk space.'
problem: Bitcoin Core cannot query transaction history by address or script without scanning blocks or tracking descriptors in the wallet, forcing node operators and wallet frontends (like Electrum servers) to run separate third-party indexing software.

risk.why: Bugs in the index database logic or serialization could cause database corruption or excessive disk reads during RPC lookups.

scope_notes: Adds an order-preserving varint serialization format and a new index implementation across 25 files.
summary: Adds an optional index `txoscriptindex` that records transaction output scripts by a 5-byte SipHash prefix of their SHA256 script hash and block height using an order-preserving integer serializer. Adds a `getscripthistory` RPC that returns output history (and spending transactions when `txospenderindex` is active) for raw scripts, addresses, or ranged descriptors, enforcing a read-byte budget to prevent runaway queries.
